spans.s:
Maṭacī occurs in a passage of the Chāndogya upaniṣad. where reference is made to the Kurus being overwhelmed by Maṭacīs. Śaṅkara interprets the word by ‘thunderbolts’ (aśanayaḥ), while Ānandatīrtha in his commentary gives, as an alternative rendering, pāṣāṇa-vṛṣṭayaḥ--i.e., ‘hailstones,’ which may be the sense. The Śabdakalpadruma, agreeing with Ānandatīrtha, says that maṭacī means, ‘a kind of small red bird’ (rakta-varṇa-kṣudra-pakṣi-viśeṣa, reading -pakṣī-), and Jacob suggests that the ‘locust’ is meant.
Foot notes i. 10, 1.
